title: First page of the Senné register volume: 'Memoria digna', the list of parish priests from 1718
extract: 'Worth remembering. The series of parish priests of the church of Szenna, as far as it could be dug out of old documents, the registers especially, after the church was recovered from the Calvinists in 1718.' Twenty-six priests follow, from Adamus Petrik to Georgius Balás (1850 to 1886), among them Stephanus Rácz, 1831 to 1841. Under Balás: windows repaired, a new organ bought; on 28 October 1865 at eleven at night something was destroyed by fire 'through a malicious man'; a bell was blessed on 20 July 1871 by Bishop László Bíró in honour of St Ladislaus, with a bell for Solymos dedicated to St Christopher. Then, in later hands: Julius Buzinkay made interim administrator; Stephanus Rusznák named administrator on 4 October 1886, invested 1887, died 3 May 1892; Buzinkay took the place on 24 July 1892 and was invested on 7 November 1894. The image carries a microfilm target reading 'Whole Volume'. Much of the lower half is at the limit of legibility and is given only in outline.

extract: A printed colour map of Ung county, drawn by Pál Gönczy, at 1:380,000, with relief, rivers, marsh, roads, the railway and the four districts outlined in red. The red district line runs between them: Solymos, Jesztreb, Rebrin and Gézsény lie in the Szobránc district, and Szenna, Pályin, Viszoka and Csicser in the Kapos district. Any record kept by district, a census among them, will have the two villages in different bundles.

type: Printed map (published source)

The image has no key to the colours; by where they fall they look like the main language of each village (Hungarian, Slovak, Ruthenian), and that is this agent's inference, not something the map says. extract: An enlarged crop of a typed passenger list of men arriving in Canada, with later notes by the immigration office. Three men in a row are from Senné, Czechoslovakia, Slovak: Andrey Dzvonik, 24; Mikulas Duska, 39; and Michal Duska, 26. The ship, the port and the date are not in the crop. Against Michal an office hand has written 'Copy on O.F. 633695' and 'Nat. 22/4/40': a copy of the entry went to file 633695, and he was naturalised on 22 April 1940. That file number is the one on the Immigration Branch letter of 1937 to Mike Duska of Montréal (D-006-11, read there as 6336[93]), so this Michal is Štefan's father. Against Mikulas: 'Nat: 21/1/46'. Between the two lines a hand has written what looks like '+ Brother'; the typed relationship column has only ditto marks under 'none'. The ages date the voyage: a man born on 3 July 1903 was 26 until July 1930, and one born on 28 November 1890 was 39 from November 1929, so they sailed between late November 1929 and early July 1930, within months of Štefan's birth. A Michal born in December 1896 would have been 33.
reliability: Typed at the time from the passengers' papers; ages are as declared. The ink notes are later office work. Reading level: medium; the word read 'Brother' is doubtful.
